items.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: I have a little quartet group that Phil Flanigan plays with

ctx.x: Do you do a certain amount of your own promotion to try to keep your name — I mean even like a place like this — do you try to make sure that the promoter doesn’t forget about you or is it not necessary? Do you think you’re in the circuit enough that —

Yeah I think so. I do a certain amount of promotion personally on certain things. Like I have a website, a web page, and I have a little quartet group that Phil Flanigan plays with, we were talking about Phil before, and a couple of guys from Florida. We try to do tributes to the things that Sidney Bechet and Muggsy Spanier did in the 40s, with just guitar and bass and cornet and clarinet. And we have been trying to promote that some more to get some more work for it, but other than that, the rest of it, a lot of…
These parties here are almost like you have your own little fan club sometimes. I see all the people come up, and, “I saw you in Sarasota” and, “would you sign this.” It’s a nice situation.
